entry.title: What's New in SAP Asset Performance Management 2610
entry.content:
SAP Asset Performance Management 2610 brings a significantly improved Monitor Alerts experience alongside a focused set of enhancements to industrial systems, configuration, and platform transparency. The rebuilt Monitor Alerts application introduces clear ownership, full change traceability, and direct integration with SAP S/4HANA - all in one place. This release also deepens the context available when working with technical objects and industrial systems, adds location-based filtering for administrators, and delivers a new troubleshooting guide to help teams resolve issues faster. There is also an important announcement about the transition away from legacy GraphQL-based applications.

Before we start, I'd like to alert you to the replay of the SAP Asset Performance Management - Product Expert Training  H2 2026 with Jan Patrick Klein, where we gave a glimpse into our upcoming agents. Watch it here.

Asset Health Monitoring

A New App for Monitoring Alerts in SAP Asset Performance Management

In 2610, SAP Asset Performance Management introduces a significantly improved Monitor Alerts experience - rebuilt on the SAP Cloud Application Programming (CAP) framework. The new application brings clear ownership, full change traceability, direct integration with SAP S/4HANA, and better context for investigation, all without leaving a single application.

We have written a dedicated blog post that walks through the full story - from the moment an alert lands in the queue to the maintenance notification raised in S/4HANA. Read it here - Introducing new 'Monitor Alerts' application in SAP Asset Performance Management.

Business Value

This gives customers:

  • Full alert investigation workflow in one place - no switching between applications or systems
  • Clear ownership with a new Assigned To field - nothing sits unattended in a shared queue
  • Complete audit trail of every alert change, automatically captured in a Change Log tab
  • Maintenance notifications created directly from the alert, with a Detection Method field to support future failure analysis
  • A foundation built for extensibility - workflows and fields can be adapted to your operation via CAP

Asset Data and Information Management

Location Details Available in Technical Objects

What if you could see the exact physical location of a technical object - and filter by it - without leaving the Explore Technical Objects application?

With this release, Room, Location, and Plant Section are now displayed directly in the Information tab of the Technical Object details page, and Location and Plant Section are available as filters in Explore Technical Objects. These fields are also exposed in the public API.

Challenge

Maintenance and reliability teams often need to locate an asset physically - not just by its ID or description. Previously, location attributes such as Room, Location, and Plant Section were not visible in SAP APM or available for filtering. Teams had to consult the source system or rely on tribal knowledge to determine where an asset was physically situated.

Solution

Room, Location, and Plant Section now appear in the Information tab of any Technical Object details page. Location and Plant Section can also be used as filters when browsing or searching technical objects. The same fields are exposed via the public API, making them available for integrations and downstream processes.

Note: This enhancement applies only to SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition and SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition 2021 FPS01 or higher.

Explore Technical Objects filter bar and results table with new Location, Plant Section, and Room fields highlighted

Key Details

  • Room, Location, and Plant Section displayed in the Technical Object Information tab
  • Location and Plant Section available as filters in Explore Technical Objects
  • Fields exposed via the public API
  • Applicable to SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition and SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition 2021 FPS01 or higher

Business Value

This gives customers:

  • Physical location context directly in SAP APM - no need to cross-reference the source system
  • Faster narrowing of technical objects by location when investigating issues or planning maintenance
  • Location data accessible via API for reporting and integration scenarios

For more information, see Viewing Data Related to a Specific Technical Object.

Industrial Systems: Better Visibility, Clearer Modelling

What if working with industrial systems felt less like switching between applications and more like having the full picture in one place?

This release brings three connected improvements to industrial systems in SAP APM. Together they make it easier to find the right system, understand how a technical object fits within it, and accurately represent planned installations in the system model.

See System Context Directly on a Technical Object

A new Industrial Systems tab is now available on every Technical Object details page in Explore Technical Objects. It lists all industrial systems the object belongs to - no need to navigate to the Manage Industrial Systems application to get that context. Whether you're investigating a failure or reviewing an asset's role in a larger system, the information is now right there where you're already working.

Released Systems Shown by Default

When selecting an industrial system from the Select Industrial Systems dialog in Explore Technical Objects, the Status filter now defaults to Released. This means the list opens showing only the systems that are ready for downstream operations - the ones you're most likely to need. You can still clear or change the filter if you need to see systems in other statuses.

Status filter is set to "Released" by default in the "Select Industrial System" dialog

Model Planned Installations as Product Occurrences

System elements in a Product Aspect hierarchy can now be marked as Product Occurrences. This designation explicitly flags a position in the hierarchy as a structural placeholder for a physical item - such as equipment or a functional location - that is planned to be installed there. In asset-intensive industries where system design precedes physical build, this gives teams a formal way to represent planned installations and keep the system model aligned with design intent.

"Manage Industrial Systems" showing a system element in the Product Aspect hierarchy with the Product Occurrence checkbox, which when marked designates a placeholder position for a planned physical item installation

Key Details

  • New Industrial Systems tab on Technical Object details pages shows all systems the object belongs to
  • Status filter in the Select Industrial Systems dialog now defaults to Released
  • System elements in Product Aspect hierarchies can be marked as Product Occurrences to represent planned installations

Business Value

These three improvements give customers:

  • Industrial system context visible directly on technical object pages - no application switching required
  • Faster selection of the right industrial system with released systems shown by default
  • A formal way to model planned installation positions in industrial system hierarchies, keeping design intent and installed asset data aligned

For more information, see Industrial Systems and Setting a System Element as a Product Occurrence.

Administration and Configuration

Plant Section and Location Filters in Configuration Manager

What if administrators could scope technical object replication by physical location - directly from Configuration Manager?

Plant Section and Location are now available as replication filters in the Configuration Manager, giving administrators finer control over which technical objects are replicated into SAP APM.

Challenge

Administrators managing large asset landscapes often need to control exactly which technical objects are replicated into SAP APM. Without location-based filter options, achieving this level of precision required workarounds or broader replication scopes than needed.

Solution

"Plant Section" and "Location" filters are now available directly in the Configuration Manager under Communication Systems. Administrators can use these filters to narrow the scope of technical object replication to specific physical areas within a plant, reducing the volume of irrelevant data and improving replication efficiency.

Configuration Manager app showing new "Plant Section" and "Location" filters under Communication Systems for technical object replication configuration

Key Details

  • Plant Section and Location available as replication filters in Configuration Manager
  • Applies to technical object replication configuration under Communication Systems
  • Allows administrators to narrow replication scope to specific physical locations

Business Value

This gives customers:

  • Precise, location-based control over technical object replication - no workarounds needed
  • Reduced replication of irrelevant objects, supporting cleaner data and better system performance
  • Administration aligned to the physical structure of the plant

For more information, see Communication Systems.

General

Troubleshooting Guide for SAP Asset Performance Management

A new troubleshooting guide is now available for SAP Asset Performance Management. Organized by feature area, it covers common issues related to application access, configuration, data integration, assessments, rule execution, and more. Each topic describes the issue, its possible causes, and recommended resolution steps.

This is a practical addition for customers and partners who want structured guidance when something isn't working as expected - without needing to raise a support ticket for every issue.

For more information, see Troubleshooting in SAP Asset Performance Management.

Important Announcement - Migration Required Before 2611

As part of the ongoing transition to Cloud Application Programming Model (CAP) based applications, support for several legacy GraphQL-based application versions has been extended to the 2611 release (November 16, 2026). After that date, these versions will be removed from the Fiori Launchpad.

The affected applications are:

  • Manage Recommendations
  • Implement Recommendations
  • Manage Risk and Criticality Assessments
  • Manage Templates for Risk and Criticality Assessments
  • Manage Strategy Assessment for Classes
  • Manage RCM Assessments
  • Manage FMEA Assessments

If your organization is still using any of these legacy versions, you must migrate to the CAP-based versions before November 16, 2026 to ensure uninterrupted service.

For release timeline details, see Release Schedule and Dates for 2026.

Stay Informed and Get Involved

  • We've recently revamped our SAP Community for APM page. Check out this one stop shop for an overview of upcoming enablement sessions, content and learning opportunities for APM. Subscribe to get notified of updates.
  • Explore our latest APM blog posts here.
  • Find out what's up and coming in the SAP Road Map Explorer.
  • For the full feature documentation for 2610, visit the SAP Help Portal.
  • Send us your improvement requests. Submit or vote for the improvement you would like to see in the SAP Continuous Influence session.
  • Check the latest update of the APM link collection.

See you for the next update! SAP Asset Performance Management

entry.title: Re: sap物料基本单位异常
entry.content:
Hello,

Thank you very much for your question.
Here is the AI-generated response. Please check whether it helps resolve the issue.

Kind regards,
Henrike

---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Joule Response

SAP S/4HANA Cloud: 物料基本单位 BAT vs PAT 区别

在 SAP 标准计量单位（UoM）体系中，BAT 和 PAT 虽然描述均显示为 "Packet"，但它们是两个独立的内部单位代码，实际含义和适用场景存在差异。以下是基于 SAP 标准 UoM 定义的区分说明：

项目 BAT PAT
内部代码BATPAT
标准描述Batch（批次/批量包）Packet（小包/零售包装单位）
单位含义通常指一个生产批次或批量包装单位，强调批量概念，常见于制造、化工、制药等行业通常指标准零售小包装单位，强调单个包装，常见于消费品、零售、仓储拣货场景
适用场景批量采购、生产领料、批次管理物料零售包装销售、仓库拣货、小包装配送

注意：SAP 系统中 UoM 的显示描述可能因语言包配置或客户化设置而出现相同描述（如均显示 "Packet"），但内部代码 BAT 与 PAT 在系统逻辑上是不同的单位。建议通过事务码 CUNI（计量单位维护）核查两者的精确定义及换算关系，以确认贵司系统中的实际配置。[1]

单位选错后的影响与建议

无法更改基本单位的限制说明

SAP 对基本计量单位（Base UoM）的变更有严格限制，只有满足以下全部条件时才允许修改 [2]：

  • 物料无现有库存
  • 不存在未删除的采购申请、采购订单或调度协议
  • 当前没有正在创建或变更中的采购订单

此外，以下情况也会阻止基本单位变更（系统将报错 M3189 或类似错误）[3] [4] [5] [6]：

  • 存在未设置删除标记的采购订单/采购申请
  • 存在已分配的独立需求
  • 存在托盘化数据（MLGN 表有记录）
  • 存在 BOM、生产订单、销售订单等业务单据

业务影响说明

  • 基本单位选错后，所有库存数量、采购数量、生产数量均以错误单位记录，导致数量换算偏差，影响库存准确性
  • 财务凭证（ACDOCA 通用日记账）中记录的数量以基本单位为准，单位错误将导致财务与业务数据不一致 [7]
  • 仓库管理（EWM/WM）中的任务单位、拣货单位均依赖基本单位换算，选错单位可能导致仓库任务数量异常 [8] [9]
  • 基本单位一旦有业务数据关联，实际上极难变更，社区实践中也有反映即使清除了 PO/PR 仍无法修改的情况 [3]

建议解决方案与规避措施

  1. 事前预防（最重要）：

    • 在物料创建前，通过 CUNI 事务码统一梳理并规范企业内部使用的计量单位，明确 BAT、PAT 等相似单位的业务定义，形成选用规范文档
    • 物料创建时强制要求业务部门确认基本单位，避免依赖系统描述文字选择单位

  2. 已选错但尚无业务数据：

    • 在无库存、无采购单据、无生产单据的前提下，进入物料主数据变更模式，直接覆盖旧基本单位并保存 [2]
    • 系统将自动校验是否满足变更条件，如不满足则显示错误原因（选择"Display Errors"查看详情）

  3. 已有业务数据无法直接变更：

    • 逐步清理阻止变更的业务单据：对采购订单/采购申请设置删除标记 [4]，删除独立需求（MD76）[5]，清除托盘化数据（MM02 WM2 视图）[6]
    • 如内部 UoM 代码本身需要替换，需先归档所有相关历史单据，参考 SAP Note 138767 和 2392688 [10]
    • 对于确实无法变更的物料，可考虑将错误物料标记删除，重新创建正确基本单位的新物料，并做好数据迁移

  4. 长期治理建议：

    • 建立物料主数据创建审批流程，基本单位字段设置为必审字段
    • 定期通过 CUNI 审查自定义计量单位，避免重复创建描述相似的单位

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition: Material Base Unit of Measure — BAT vs PAT
Distinguishing BAT and PAT Unit Codes

In SAP's Unit of Measure (UoM) framework, both BAT and PAT may display similar descriptions (e.g., "Packet") depending on system language settings, but they are distinct internal unit codes with different intended meanings and use cases.

Item BAT PAT
Internal CodeBATPAT
Standard MeaningBatch — refers to a production batch or bulk packaging unit, emphasizing a batch/lot conceptPacket — refers to a standard retail small-package unit, emphasizing individual packaging
Typical IndustryManufacturing, chemicals, pharmaceuticals (batch-managed materials)Consumer goods, retail, warehouse picking, small-package distribution
Applicable ScenarioBulk procurement, production goods issue, batch-managed stockRetail packaging sales, warehouse picking, small-package delivery

Note: In SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, the display description of a UoM may appear identical across codes due to language pack configuration or client-specific settings. The internal codes BAT and PAT are, however, logically distinct units within the system. It is recommended to verify the precise definitions and conversion factors of both units via the CUNI transaction (Unit of Measure Maintenance) to confirm the actual configuration in your system. [1]

Why the Base Unit of Measure Cannot Be Changed After Business Data Exists

SAP enforces strict restrictions on changing the Base Unit of Measure (Base UoM) once business data is associated with a material. A change is only permitted when all of the following conditions are met:

  • No existing stock for the material
  • No open or undeleted purchase requisitions, purchase orders, or scheduling agreements
  • No active production orders, sales orders, or BOM assignments
  • No warehouse management (EWM/WM) palletization data (MLGN table records)

If any of these conditions are not met, the system will block the change and display an error (e.g., message M3189 or similar). [2]

Business Impact of Selecting the Wrong Base Unit
  • Inventory accuracy: All stock quantities, procurement quantities, and production quantities are recorded in the base unit — an incorrect unit causes quantity conversion discrepancies
  • Financial accounting: The universal journal (ACDOCA) records quantities in the base unit; a wrong unit leads to inconsistencies between financial and operational data
  • Warehouse management: EWM/WM task quantities and picking units depend on base unit conversions — an incorrect base unit may cause warehouse task quantity anomalies
  • Language/description confusion: As noted in SAP KBA 3762200, UoM descriptions are language-dependent [1]; similar descriptions across different UoM codes (like BAT and PAT) increase the risk of selection errors during material creation
Recommended Solutions and Preventive Measures

1. Prevention (Most Important)

  • Before creating materials, use CUNI to review and standardize all UoM codes in use — clearly define the business meaning of similar-looking units such as BAT and PAT, and publish an internal selection guideline
  • Make the Base UoM field subject to mandatory business confirmation during material creation to avoid reliance on system description text alone

2. If the Wrong Unit Was Selected but No Business Data Exists Yet

  • In the material master change mode (MM02), directly overwrite the old base unit and save
  • The system will automatically validate whether all change conditions are met; if not, it will display the specific blocking reason (choose "Display Errors" to review details)

3. If Business Data Already Exists and Direct Change Is Blocked

  • Systematically clear the blocking business documents: set deletion flags on purchase orders/purchase requisitions, clear palletization data (MM02, WM2 view)
  • For cases where the internal UoM code itself needs replacement, all related historical documents must first be archived; refer to SAP Notes 138767 and 2392688 for guidance
  • For materials where the base unit truly cannot be changed, consider marking the incorrect material for deletion, creating a new material with the correct base unit, and performing data migration

4. Long-Term Data Governance

  • Establish a material master creation approval workflow with the Base UoM field designated as a mandatory review field
  • Periodically audit custom UoM entries via CUNI to prevent duplicate creation of units with similar descriptions [1]

entry.title: How I Built an Interactive Executive Dashboard Overnight
entry.content:
Every program manager knows the pain: you send a weekly update email, it gets read once, then buried. Important trends live across five different emails. When someone asks "what was the case count three weeks ago?" you're digging through your inbox.

I had exactly this problem, So I challenged myself: turn months of email updates into a single, navigatable, self-contained dashboard in one evening.

Here's exactly how I did it and how you can too.

What I Ended Up With

A single HTML file. No server. No database. No deployment pipeline. Just one file you can open in any browser, share via email, or host on SharePoint. It includes:

  • Tab navigation across multiple update dates
  • A live trend chart (case volume over time) - click a data point to jump directly to that date's full update
  • Cross-section links  - clicking a case count jumps you to the overview summary; clicking a topic title jumps to the relevant detail card
  • Back buttons on every date tab so you never feel lost
  • The official SAP logo rendered in pure SVG no image files needed
  • Real external links wired to ServiceNow, AHA!, SharePoint, and GitHub Pages resources

The Stack

Layer What I used Why

StructurePlain HTMLWorks everywhere, no framework needed
StylingInline CSS with CSS variablesOne file, easy to theme
ChartsChart.js (CDN)Minimal setup, great interactivity
NavigationVanilla JavaScript3 functions, ~30 lines total
HostingLocal file / SharePointZero infrastructure

The entire navigation system is three JavaScript functions:

// Switch to a tab
function goTo(id) { ... }

// Switch to a tab AND scroll to a specific element (with a pulse highlight)
function goToAnchor(tabId, anchorId) { ... }

// Original tab show (wired to tab buttons)
function show(id, el) { ... }

The One Design Decision That Made Everything Better

Instead of linking out to external tools for every click, I built within-page navigation first. Clicking "Total Open Cases" doesn't open ServiceNow  it scrolls you to the overview trend table for that date. This means the dashboard is fully usable offline and in any SharePoint environment where external links might be blocked.

External links are additive, not load-bearing.

What You Can Reuse

If you want to build something similar for your own program:

  • Start with your email cadence. If you send weekly updates, you already have the content you just need structure.
  • One tab per update, one overview tab with a trend chart. That's the whole architecture.
  • CSS variables for theming. Swap --blue: #0070F2 to your program's colour and you are rebranded.
  • The three JS navigation functions above are copy-paste ready. Add id="your-section" to any element you want to link to, then call goToAnchor('tab-id', 'your-section') from anywhere.

The Bigger Point

We talk a lot about AI accelerating development for engineers. But the real unlock is for non-engineers who know their domain deeply program managers, solution advisors, business analysts. You don't need to learn HTML to build something like this. You need to know what you want clearly enough to describe it. That's a skill most of us already have.

entry.title: Re: SAP ECC to S4 Hana Public Cloud Migration
entry.content:
Hello,

Thank you very much for your question.

Here's the AI-generated response. Please check whether it helps you resolve the issue.

Kind regards,

Henrike

SAP ECC TCode to S/4HANA Tile Mapping

Great question for your ECC to S/4HANA Public Cloud migration! There is no single centralized list that maps all ECC transaction codes to their corresponding S/4HANA Fiori tiles — this is a known gap. However, SAP provides several official tools and approaches to build this mapping. [1]

Recommended Approaches

1. SAP Fiori Apps Reference Library (Primary Tool)

The SAP Fiori Apps Reference Library is the most reliable way to find the mapping between ECC TCodes and S/4HANA Fiori tiles. [2] [3]

Step-by-step to get the mapping list:

  1. Go to: https://fioriappslibrary.hana.ondemand.com/sap/fix/externalViewer/
  2. Select "All Apps for SAP S/4HANA Cloud" on the left-hand side [3]
  3. Filter by Line of Business (e.g., Finance, Procurement, Sales)
  4. Switch to "List View" at the bottom of the page
  5. Click the column settings (star wheel icon) on the top right and add the "Transaction" field — this reveals the corresponding ECC TCode for each Fiori app [3]
  6. Use the "Download" button to export the full list to Excel for your migration documentation

⚠️ Important caveat: The mapping is not always 1-to-1. In some cases, one ECC TCode is split into several Fiori apps; in other cases, multiple ECC TCodes are merged into a single Fiori app. [3] [4]

2. Fiori App Recommendations (Upload Your TCode List)

entry.title: Re: Returns delivery shared as outbound in 1ZQ scope item
entry.content:
Hello,

Thank you very much for your question.

Here is the AI-generated response. Please check whether it helps you resolve the issue.

Kind regards,

Henrike

Return Delivery in Outbound Queue – 1ZQ Scope Item
Observation

In SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition with scope item 1ZQ (Logistics with Third-Party Warehouse Management), when return deliveries are set up to be processed by the 3PL warehouse, the return delivery document ends up in the outbound delivery message queue/event mesh — rather than an inbound delivery queue. This feels counterintuitive, since the physical goods movement is inbound (goods being received back into the warehouse). [1]

Root Cause

This behavior is by design within the 1ZQ integration architecture. The key principle is:

If the third-party WMS managed storage location is the sending location, an outbound delivery Web Services message is created. If it is the receiving location, an inbound delivery Web Services message is created.

For a Return to Supplier scenario, the 3PL-managed storage location acts as the sending location (goods are physically leaving the warehouse to go back to the supplier). Therefore, the system generates an outbound delivery IDoc/Web Services message — which is the correct technical classification from the WMS integration perspective, even though from a procurement/returns perspective it may feel like a "receipt." [2] [3]

For Customer Returns, the same logic applies in reverse: the WMS receives the goods, so an outbound delivery IDoc/Web Services message is still used for the returns delivery, and the WMS then sends back an outbound delivery confirmation. [3] [4]

The 1ZQ scope item uses the SHP_OBDLV_SAVE_REPLICA IDoc (or equivalent SOAP API) to communicate return delivery information to the third-party WMS, which then creates an outbound delivery request, picks and ships to the supplier, and upon goods issue posts confirmation back to SAP S/4HANA Cloud. [4]

Resolution Options

  1. SAP Standard Behavior – No Configuration Change Available This routing of return deliveries into the outbound message queue is the standard, designed behavior of the 1ZQ integration. There is currently no configuration switch or SAP-delivered workaround to reroute return deliveries into a separate or "inbound" queue within the 1ZQ SOAP/IDoc framework. The 1ZQ scope item's interface list does not include a dedicated "return delivery inbound" message type — all delivery-to-WMS communication flows through the outbound delivery Web Services channel. [5] [2]

  2. Integration-Layer Handling Approach As you have already identified, the recommended path is to handle this distinction within your integration layer. You can differentiate return deliveries from standard outbound deliveries by inspecting delivery-type or document attributes in the message payload (e.g., delivery type RL for Return to Supplier, or specific movement type 161). Your integration middleware can then route or process these messages differently based on those attributes, even though they arrive via the same outbound delivery queue/event mesh topic. [6] [7]

Recommendation
  • Short term: Continue with your current integration-layer approach of distinguishing return deliveries from standard outbound deliveries based on delivery type or movement type attributes in the message. This is the pragmatic and supported path within the current 1ZQ design. [3]
  • Medium term: If this behavior represents a significant business pain point, it is advisable to submit a Feature Request through SAP's official channel, clearly describing the business use case (return deliveries requiring a distinct message queue/topic from standard outbound deliveries) and the expected value. Feature requests are evaluated separately from incidents and feed into SAP's product roadmap consideration. [8]
  • For reference: Review the 1ZQ test scripts on SAP Help Portal (help.sap.com) for the "Return to Supplier" process variant to confirm the exact API/IDoc types in use for your specific sub-scenario, and check the SAP API Hub (api.sap.com) for any newer SOAP API variants that may offer finer-grained message categorization. [5] [2]

entry.title: Re: FM GUI_DOWNLOAD dump RAISE_EXCEPTION - NOT_SUPPORTED_BY_GUI
entry.content:
If the function module GUI_DOWNLOAD is called with the importing parameter CONFIRM_OVERWRITE or APPEND set to 'X' (it's called also via CL_GUI_FRONTEND_SERVICES=>GUI_DOWNLOAD), the method CL_GUI_FRONTEND_SERVICES=>FILE_EXIST is called by the function module without handling its exceptions so there's a short dump. Here's the culprit code in the function module GUI_DOWNLOAD:

IF NOT CONFIRM_OVERWRITE IS INITIAL OR NOT APPEND IS INITIAL.
  PRC_RESULT = CL_GUI_FRONTEND_SERVICES=>FILE_EXIST( FILENAME ).

The solution is:

  • either to fix the standard code inside the function module GUI_DOWNLOAD by handling the possible exceptions raised by FILE_EXIST (including NOT_SUPPORTED_BY_GUI),
  • or to change the custom program to not call GUI_DOWNLOAD (FM or method) if GUI is not supported by calling the method CL_GUI_FRONTEND_SERVICES=>CHECK_GUI_SUPPORT (that will detect any non-dialog process like a background job, etc.)

Sandra

NB: the bug exists at least in ABAP 7.58 SP 1 and I didn't find any SAP Note about it.

entry.title: Re: How are bank sub-accounts (clearing accounts) cleared?
entry.content:
Hi,

In this setup, the bank reconciliation account holds the confirmed bank balance, and the bank subaccount is the clearing account for payments in transfer. The subaccount is managed on an open item basis, and how it is cleared depends on which document comes first.

1. Outgoing payments (payment first, bank statement later)
- Payment entry (payment run or outgoing payment): Dr Vendor / Cr Bank subaccount. This clears the vendor and creates an open item on the subaccount.
- Bank statement: Dr Bank subaccount / Cr Bank reconciliation account. This clears the subaccount.

2. Incoming receipts (bank statement first, receipt later)
- Bank statement: Dr Bank reconciliation account / Cr Bank subaccount, when the customer cannot be identified automatically.
- Receipt posting (bank statement post-processing): Dr Bank subaccount / Cr Customer. This clears the subaccount and the customer.

Clearing methods
1. Electronic bank statement with interpretation algorithms (main method): the system uses the reference returned by the bank to find and clear the open item, for example 020 (document number search), 021 (reference number search), 019 (DME reference) or 011/012/013 for checks.
2. Bank statement reprocessing: statement items that could not be matched are cleared manually by selecting the open item.
3. Automatic G/L clearing job: remaining items are cleared using clearing criteria such as Assignment or Reference with a zero balance.
4. Manual G/L clearing: for any items still open.

 

Hope this helps.

entry.title: Implementing Dynamic Approvals in SAP SmartRecruiter
entry.content:
The Problem: Static Approval Chains

By default, SmartRecruiter allows you to configure Sequential or Parallel approval chains where the list of approvers is fixed at configuration time. This works well for homogeneous workflows, but breaks down when business rules require different approvers based on runtime data.

Two scenarios that call for dynamic routing:

  • Job approval: If the total compensation package is >= 100 (e.g., LPA), it must be approved by User A and User B; otherwise, by User A and User C.
  • Offer approval: If the salary hike is <= 50%, approvers are A and B; if 50–100%, approvers are A, B, and C; if > 100%, approvers are A, B, and the Head of Department.

These rules cannot be pre-configured statically. The solution is an Integration-type approval chain that delegates control to an external CPI flow at runtime.

Setting Up an Integration-Type Approval Chain in SmartRecruiter

Navigate to Settings > Job Approvals in SmartRecruiter and create a new approval chain. Instead of selecting Sequential or Parallel, choose the Integration tab. This tells SmartRecruiter that an external integration (your CPI iFlow) is responsible for managing the approval process.

Inside the chain configuration, set the Approval Chain type to Integration and select your registered CPI application as the App Integration. All scope fields can be set to 'All selected' for a global rule or scoped down as needed.

Key concept: When an Integration-type chain is active, SmartRecruiter assigns a system/integration user as the initial placeholder approver. This user acts as a signal to your CPI flow that the approval needs to be re-assigned dynamically.

What Happens When a Job Is Created

Once the integration chain is active, creating a new job in SmartRecruiter will automatically route the approval to the configured integration user (system user). The job moves into a 'Pending approval' state.

The webhook event job.approval.created fires at this point, triggering your CPI iFlow to take over the approval routing.

Implementing Dynamic Approval Logic in CPI

Your CPI iFlow receives the job.approval.created webhook payload. A Groovy script within the flow reads the relevant job or offer fields, evaluates the business rules, and determines the correct approvers. The implementation follows two API calls to SmartRecruiter.

Step 1: Get the Current Approval (Retrieve baseId)

Call the following endpoint to retrieve the latest approval for the job:

GET https://api.smartrecruiters.com/jobs/{jobId}/approvals/latest

The response includes the approvalRequestId which becomes the baseId for the next call.

Step 2: Create a New Approval with Dynamic Approvers

POST to the Approvals API with the baseId and the dynamically determined approver list:

POST https://api.smartrecruiters.com/approvals-api/v201910/approvals

Request Body:

{
  "baseId": "35a1ef73-4542-4d37-84c2-2b34522327e1",
  "type": "sequential",
  "decisionMode": "any",
  "steps": [
    {
      "approvers": [
        { "id": "6a986436be2958fa852dda78" }   // User A
      ]
    },
    {
      "approvers": [
        { "id": "6a98643697a14f8c43c2a454" }   // User B or C (from Groovy logic)
      ]
    }
  ]
}

Verifying the Dynamic Approval on the SmartRecruiter UI

After the CPI iFlow completes the POST call, refresh the job in SmartRecruiter. The approval panel will now show the dynamically assigned approvers — replacing the original integration user with the correct business approvers as determined by the Groovy logic.

Triggering the Integration via Webhook

The entire flow is event-driven. Configure a SmartRecruiter webhook to fire your CPI iFlow endpoint whenever a job or offer approval is created.

For Job Approvals — subscribe to:

For Offer Approvals — subscribe to:

Extending to Offer Approvals

The exact same pattern applies to offer approvals. The only differences are:

  • GET endpoint to fetch the baseId:
    https://api.smartrecruiters.com/candidates/{id}/jobs/{jobId}/offers/{offerId}/approvals/latest
  • Webhook event: offer.approval.created (instead of job.approval.created).
  • The POST endpoint and request body structure remain identical.

Tip: Reuse the same CPI iFlow for both job and offer approvals by routing on the webhook event type at the message entry point. A single Groovy script can contain all business-rule branches, keyed on the approval subject type ('job' vs 'offer') in the GET response.

Conclusion

The Integration-type approval chain in SAP SmartRecruiter, combined with the Approvals API and SAP CPI, provides a clean, scalable pattern for implementing dynamic, condition-driven approval workflows. Instead of creating dozens of static chains to cover every business scenario, you centralise the routing logic in a single CPI iFlow and let the API handle the assignment at runtime.

This approach is equally applicable to re-triggering rejected approvals — simply listen for the approval-rejected webhook, run your re-routing logic, and POST a fresh approval using the same baseId.

I hope this blog gives you a clear blueprint to get started. Feel free to share your questions or experiences in the comments below!

Thanks

Kunal

entry.title: Free Joule Studio certification (C_JSD): how to claim it and plan the 24 hours (EN/PT)
entry.content:
Versão em português mais abaixo.

English version

Hi everyone,

A certification exam where you don't pick A, B or C. You build an AI agent and then show it to an AI avatar that asks you questions about what you built. And this time the attempt is free.

That is the new SAP Certified - Joule Studio Developer, exam code C_JSD. SAP Learning published the official announcement here in the Community today (link at the end), and the offer is also on the SAP TechEd page of SAP Learning. I shared a short version of this on LinkedIn. This is the full one, with every detail checked on SAP's own pages today, October 27, 2026.

What you get

  • One free attempt per person, valid through December 31, 2026. You can sign up only once.
  • No SAP Learning Hub subscription, no certification purchase, no BTP subaccount and no Joule Studio subscription. SAP gives you a pre-configured Joule Studio practice system.
  • Open to anyone with an SAP Universal ID. The FAQ says there is no restriction based on company type, role or geography.

How the exam works

It is performance-based. First you complete the hands-on exercises in the practice system, and that part is mandatory. Then comes the scenario-based assessment: an AI roleplay where an avatar asks you to show the agents you built and answer questions about them.

  • The certification page lists 2 hours and a 60% pass score.
  • AI roleplay languages: English, Spanish, Italian, French and Japanese. No Portuguese, which matters for us in Brazil.
  • There is a non-AI alternative: you record a video answering the open questions. English only, reviewed by people, and the result can take up to 20 business days. With the AI roleplay the result usually comes right after you submit, or shortly after.
  • What it validates, according to SAP: turning a business idea into a deployable agent (intent-based development), building and extending agents, grounding them in SAP business context, and managing deployment and lifecycle.

The detail that matters most: the 24 hours

From the FAQ: "After enrolling to the practice system, you have 24h to complete the tasks and the exam." The exercises and the exam have to fit in the same 24 hours.

So the clock does not start when you claim the voucher. It starts when you enter the practice system. My advice: claim it now, study first, and only open the practice system on a day you can really dedicate to it.

Step by step

  1. Check your SAP Universal ID (you can create one for free at account.sap.com). The FAQ asks for two different email accounts assigned to it. Fix that before you start.
  2. Open the campaign page (link at the end), log in with your SAP Universal ID and accept the Terms and Conditions. The attempt is assigned to your account.
  3. Study the learning journey (next section). Don't open the practice system yet.
  4. Go through the Technical Readiness Checklist (browser, connection), linked on the certification page.
  5. On your free day: enroll in the practice system and finish all the exercises.
  6. Still inside the 24 hours: go to the certification page, find the Joule Studio certification and click "Start exam". No scheduling needed.
  7. If you pass, the badge and the certificate show up in the Certification section of your SAP Learning profile.

What to study

  • The learning journey "Developing with Joule Studio": what Joule Studio is and where it sits in the SAP Business AI Platform, then creating agents, extending existing agents and building n8n workflows inside Joule Studio. The FAQ says completing it is "strongly recommended".
  • The journey lists "Understanding AI" as a prerequisite. If AI agents are new to you, start there.
  • The scenario-based assessment FAQ, so you know what the AI roleplay looks like before you face it.

If it doesn't work out

It is a real exam, with one attempt. A failed campaign attempt does not count against your commercial attempt limits, but you cannot sign up for the campaign again. After it ends, you can buy an attempt or use the ones you already have, from January 1, 2027.

If SAP changes any rule, the FAQ wins over this post. If you already took it, tell me in the comments how your 24 hours went. I'm curious about the roleplay part.

Versão em português

Oi, pessoal,

Uma prova de certificação em que você não marca A, B ou C. Você constrói um agente de IA e depois mostra ele para um avatar de IA que faz perguntas sobre o que você construiu. E desta vez a tentativa é gratuita.

É a nova SAP Certified - Joule Studio Developer, código C_JSD. A SAP Learning publicou hoje o anúncio oficial aqui na Community (link no fim), e a oferta também está na página do SAP TechEd no SAP Learning. Postei uma versão curta no LinkedIn. Esta é a completa, com cada detalhe conferido hoje, 27/10/2026, nas páginas da própria SAP.

O que você ganha

  • Uma tentativa gratuita por pessoa, válida até 31/12/2026. Só dá para se inscrever uma vez.
  • Não precisa de assinatura do SAP Learning Hub, nem comprar prova, nem subconta de BTP, nem assinatura do Joule Studio. A SAP entrega um ambiente de prática do Joule Studio já configurado.
  • Aberta a qualquer pessoa com SAP Universal ID. A FAQ diz que não há restrição por tipo de empresa, função ou país.

Como é a prova

É prática. Primeiro você faz os exercícios no ambiente de prática, e essa parte é obrigatória. Depois vem a avaliação por cenário: um roleplay com IA em que um avatar pede para você mostrar os agentes que construiu e responder perguntas sobre eles.

  • A página da certificação informa 2 horas e nota de aprovação de 60%.
  • Idiomas do roleplay com IA: inglês, espanhol, italiano, francês e japonês. Português não está na lista, então para nós fica inglês ou espanhol.
  • Existe a alternativa sem IA: você grava um vídeo respondendo às perguntas abertas. Só em inglês, avaliado por pessoas, e o resultado pode levar até 20 dias úteis. No roleplay com IA o resultado costuma sair logo depois do envio, ou pouco depois.
  • O que ela valida, segundo a SAP: transformar uma ideia de negócio num agente pronto para implantar (desenvolvimento por intenção), criar e estender agentes, ancorar esses agentes no contexto de negócio SAP e cuidar da implantação e do ciclo de vida.

O detalhe que mais importa: as 24 horas

Da FAQ: "After enrolling to the practice system, you have 24h to complete the tasks and the exam." Os exercícios e a prova têm de caber nas mesmas 24 horas.

Ou seja, o relógio não começa quando você pega o voucher. Ele começa quando você entra no ambiente de prática. Meu conselho: garanta a vaga agora, estude antes e só abra o ambiente num dia em que você consiga se dedicar de verdade.

Passo a passo

  1. Confira o seu SAP Universal ID (dá para criar de graça em account.sap.com). A FAQ pede dois e-mails diferentes cadastrados nele. Acerte isso antes de começar.
  2. Abra a página da campanha (link no fim), entre com o SAP Universal ID e aceite os Termos e Condições. A tentativa fica atribuída à sua conta.
  3. Estude a trilha (próxima seção). Ainda não abra o ambiente de prática.
  4. Passe pelo Technical Readiness Checklist (navegador, conexão), que está na página da certificação.
  5. No dia livre: entre no ambiente de prática e termine todos os exercícios.
  6. Ainda dentro das 24 horas: vá até a página da certificação, ache a certificação Joule Studio e clique em "Start exam". Não precisa agendar.
  7. Aprovado, o badge e o certificado aparecem na seção Certification do seu perfil no SAP Learning.

O que estudar

  • A trilha "Developing with Joule Studio": o que é o Joule Studio e onde ele fica na SAP Business AI Platform, depois criar agentes, estender agentes existentes e montar workflows de n8n dentro do Joule Studio. A FAQ diz que concluir a trilha é "strongly recommended".
  • A trilha traz "Understanding AI" como pré-requisito. Se agente de IA é novidade para você, comece por ele.
  • A FAQ da avaliação por cenário, para saber como é o roleplay antes de encarar.

Se não der certo

É prova de verdade, com uma tentativa. Reprovação na tentativa da campanha não conta no seu limite de tentativas pagas, mas não dá para se inscrever na campanha de novo. Depois que ela acabar, você pode comprar uma tentativa ou usar as que já tem, a partir de 01/01/2027.

Se a SAP mudar alguma regra, vale a FAQ, não este post. Se você já fez, conta nos comentários como foram as suas 24 horas. Estou curioso com a parte do roleplay.

entry.title: What I Learned Moving an Acquired Workforce from Workday to SuccessFactors: 12 Lessons
entry.content:
What I Learned Moving an Acquired Workforce from Workday to SuccessFactors: 12 Lessons

What to plan for when moving an acquired company's employees onto a new HR system

Moving an acquired company's employees to a new HR system sounds simple: copy the data and hit a deadline. In practice, the system is often the easy part. The hard parts are outside vendors, agreements with the seller, other projects going live at the same time, and things people assumed but never checked.

This lists twelve areas to plan for. They come from moving an acquired workforce onto SAP SuccessFactors.

At a glance

#

Area

What can go wrong

What to do

1

Different vendors

The acquired company uses other payroll, time, and benefits providers.

Decide who moves to the parent's vendors and who stays. Lock in vendor dates.

2

Seller agreement (TSA)

The seller may still run some services, so some employees must not go to new vendors yet.

Add a filter by employee group and test it. Plan when it ends.

3

Logins ready early

If accounts are made after the data load, people cannot get in on day one.

Create accounts before go-live. Test a first login.

4

Software updates

The software vendor updates twice a year, and updates can change what you tested.

Put update dates on the plan. Re-test after each one.

5

Other parent projects

The parent may switch other tools on the same date.

List the overlaps. Agree what comes first. Prepare the help desk.

6

Business keeps moving

Hires and changes continue during the move.

Set a freeze period. Plan a final load for late changes.

7

Year-end timing

A January go-live clashes with payroll year-end and holidays.

Check who is available. Plan extra support over the holidays.

8

Languages

The parent's system and documents may lack the acquired company's languages.

Check language support early. Translate legal items first.

9

Training

Training is the first thing cut when time is short.

Train managers first. Keep it short and by role.

10

New countries and policies

The parent may never have set up some of the countries.

Use a checklist for each country.

11

"Closed" is not "confirmed"

Items marked closed may rest on assumptions.

Call an item closed only when both teams confirm it in the system.

12

Approvals and data loads

Legal approvals and loading side effects can move the date.

Treat approvals as must-haves. Check numbers after every test load.

PART 1

Vendors and connections

1   Different vendors

In short: The acquired company rarely uses the same vendors as the parent.

  • Payroll. This is the most sensitive area. Decide early whether employees move to the parent's payroll provider on day one, stay with their current one, or move country by country. Staying is often safest for the first pay runs, but it means building and testing an extra connection.
  • Time tracking. Hours worked drive pay. If shift rules or extra pay rates do not match, pay will be wrong.
  • Vendor availability. Each extra vendor is a team you do not control. Get named people and test dates in writing, and keep a backup plan.
  • Vendor setup. Security checks and access approvals can take longer than the build itself.

2   The seller agreement decides who goes where

In short: A Transition Services Agreement (TSA) means the seller keeps providing some services, such as payroll or benefits, for a set time.

  • Use a filter. A simple rule, such as a flag, decides which employees are sent to which vendor, and when that changes.
  • Test both ways. Add the filter to every connection. Check who is sent and who is not.
  • Plan the end. When the TSA ends, the filter is removed. Treat that as its own go-live.

Without this, someone may be paid twice, not paid at all, or sent to a vendor they should not be in.

3   Logins must be ready before go-live

In short: People cannot log in if their accounts do not exist yet.

  • Create accounts early. If access depends on the company's login system, such as Active Directory or single sign-on, accounts may not exist when the data arrives. Create them before the data load.
  • Know the login method. Whether people sign in with the company login or a password decides who fixes lockouts and resets.
  • Test as a real employee. Try the first login the way an employee would, not as an administrator.
  • Agree on names. Settle usernames, email formats, and whether employee IDs stay the same.

PART 2

Timing and change

4   Software updates follow their own calendar

In short: Updates can change features you already tested.

Cloud software like SuccessFactors gets major updates twice a year, and the dates will not match your project plan. On this project, an update affected the performance module [add your specific example here].

  • Put update dates on the project calendar from the start.
  • Re-test what already worked after each update.
  • Give one person the job of reading the release notes.

5   Other projects at the parent go live too

In short: Your go-live date is rarely the only change.

The parent may switch other tools on the same date, for example moving the employee help desk from Employee Central Service Center to ServiceNow, or changing a payroll provider.

  • List the overlaps. Find where the other projects touch yours, such as ticket types, workflows, connections, and links employees use.
  • Decide what comes first. If one change slips, agree which has priority and who decides.
  • Prepare support. Make sure acquired employees know where to send requests on day one, with help articles and trained agents.
  • Share one calendar. Everyone should see freeze periods, test dates, and announcements from other projects.
  • Watch shared people. The same experts, testers, and approvers are often needed by both projects.

6   The business does not stop during the move

In short: Hires, exits, promotions, and team changes keep happening.

  • Set a freeze. Stop changes in the old system for a short time, and decide how to handle changes made during it.
  • Plan a final load. Catch changes made after the last data copy.
  • Watch recent changes. Promotions, transfers, and pay changes with dates close to go-live are easy to miss.
  • Name an owner. Decide who enters anything that falls through by hand.

7   Go-live often lands on year-end

In short: A January 1 go-live collides with payroll year-end, tax reports, and holidays.

  • Check people's availability over the go-live weekend and the days after.
  • Check vendor freezes. Many vendors stop changes around year-end.
  • Plan extra support around holiday cover, not the usual work calendar.

PART 3

People and experience

8   Languages: the acquired company may have more than the parent

In short: The parent's system and documents may not cover every language the acquired company uses.

  • Check language support in screens, forms, and notices for every country. Gaps tend to show up late.
  • Translate the important items first: privacy notices, offer letters, policies, and how-to guides.
  • Have a native speaker review translations, especially legal wording.
  • Remember works councils often ask for translated materials before they can review.

9   Training gets squeezed

In short: Training is usually the first thing cut, yet employees and managers must work in the new system.

  • Train managers first. They answer most questions and run processes like performance and onboarding.
  • Keep it short. Quick guides, short videos, and live walk-throughs beat long courses.
  • Time it well. Training too early is forgotten, and too late does not help.
  • Cover all time zones and languages, and record sessions for people who cannot attend.
  • Offer extra support after go-live. Daily open sessions in the first weeks catch what training missed.

10   New countries, policies, and default settings

In short: The acquired company may have employees in countries the parent has never set up.

  • New country setup needs local fields, templates, and legal checks.
  • Policy gaps are common, such as a time-off policy for a country where the parent has none. That can mean tracking by hand or buying a tool.
  • Default settings can quietly cause errors, such as working hours for new hires or end-of-employment steps.
  • Systems do not match one-to-one. Understand the idea first, then match the fields.

PART 4

Control and quality

11   "Closed" is not the same as "confirmed"

In short: An item marked closed in a sign-off deck may rest on an assumption nobody checked.

One team may assume a setting is handled, while the other assumes the first team will set it up and test it.

  • Call an item closed only when both teams confirm it in the system.
  • Name one owner each for build, test, and sign-off.
  • Walk through the setup together before sign-off, especially country-specific fields and drop-down lists.
  • If a gap shows up late, start with the facts and the fix, then check what else was closed the same way.

12   Legal approvals and data loads can move the date

In short: Some of the most important items are not technical.

  • Works councils. In countries such as Germany, an employee representative body may need to be informed, consulted, or give approval before employee data moves. Treat approval as a must-have for go-live.
  • Offer letters and contract templates. They need legal review for the new employer and local law. If the hiring tool's build waits on that review, so does its testing.
  • Data loading side effects. Counters that create codes automatically can fall out of step when records are loaded with codes already filled in. Changes to drop-down lists need a plan for existing records. Mass changes can trigger messages and files to other systems. Check the numbers after every test load.
